Consumer sentiment fell 8% in August compared to last month, according to preliminary data from the University of Michigan Surveys of Consumers. Released Friday, the latest sentiment reading ended two consecutive months of improvement as Americans feel the effects of the Iran war pushing up fuel, energy and food prices.
results.title: Consumer sentiment and retail spending are down, new data shows

results.content: The decline was broad-based. While views of personal finances saw only minor changes, expected business conditions sank 11% for the short run and 17% for the long run, according to the survey. The Index of Consumer Expectations fell to 50.6 from 55.4, and the Current Economic Conditions Index dropped to 51.8 from 54.8. [...] Joanne Hsu, director of the University of Michigan Surveys of Consumers, said sentiment fell across the political spectrum, with Republicans recording the steepest month-to-month drop. U.S. consumer sentiment weakened materially in August from July as consumers worried about rising living costs due to the conflict in the Middle East, a survey showed Friday. A separate report from the U.S. Census Bureau on Friday showed that U.S. retail sales posted their first month-on-month decline in nine months.
